title: Introduce micro-agent contract simulator and constrained-output quickstart
author: Carmen Liu
release_notes: Adds a compact micro-agent quickstart demonstrating structured-output contracts, a local tool simulator for failure/loss-injection, and a lightweight lint/test harness for output contracts.
description:
Motivation: Teams frequently build small agent-like orchestrators that call tools and must validate structured outputs from models and tools. Existing RAG/agent examples focus on orchestration at scale but lack a compact, testable pattern for enforcing JSON-schema contracts and simulating tool failures locally. This PR adds a self-contained quickstart that demonstrates: 1) defining JSON Schema contracts for tool responses and model structured output; 2) an opinionated 'structlinter' that validates outputs during dev + CI; 3) a lightweight tool simulator that can inject latency, error responses, and partial payloads to exercise fallback logic; 4) micro-agent stubs in Python and TypeScript with contract-aware decoding and graceful fallback; 5) a VS Code devcontainer and a GitHub Actions pipeline to run schema tests and an end-to-end smoke run.

What I changed (high-level):
- New quickstart under redwood-examples/micro-agent-contract-quickstart containing README, samples, and test harness.
- Added JSON schemas under schemas/output-contract.json and schemas/tool-responses.json with examples and edge-case fixtures.
- Implemented structlinter (tools/structlinter/) as a tiny CLI that loads schemas and asserts model/tool outputs; included unit tests.
- Tool simulator (tools/simulator/) to run a local HTTP stub that responds according to fixture scenarios (ok / slow / malformed / partial). The simulator is designed to be easily wired into the devcontainer for local interactive runs.
- Example micro-agents: python-agent/main.py (async sample using Redwood SDK patterns), ts-agent/index.ts (fetch + structured parsing + fallback to a search tool).
- CI: .github/workflows/quickstart-ci.yml runs formatting, structlinter tests, and a small Playwright-based scenario that runs the simulator and exercises the agent in a containerized environment.
- Devcontainer: devcontainer.json + Dockerfile with preinstalled tooling (poetry, node, rust for wasm stubs) for easy onboarding.

CI history: initial run (2025-01-11) failed on formatting (black/ruff) and TS type check; fixed in 2nd commit; final run (2025-01-14) passed all jobs (format, unit tests, structlinter, smoke e2e). CI log summary: formatting fixes applied automatically, unit tests 12 passed, structlinter checks 6 passed, smoke runner 1 e2e scenario passed (simulator slow-path + fallback exercised).

Testing notes and how to run locally: The README contains a single-command bootstrap that starts the simulator and runs the Python agent against the 'malformed' and 'slow' scenarios. Structlinter can be run via tools/structlinter/cli.py --schema schemas/output-contract.json --fixtures fixtures/. The devcontainer is prewired to expose port 9001 for the simulator and mounts the example code for iterative editing.

Rationale/Design choices: keep the quickstart intentionally small (one schema, two tools, two agent languages) so it can be used as a lab exercise in workshops while also serving as a copy-pastable pattern. The structlinter is intentionally minimal and focused on developer ergonomics rather than being a full schema-fuzzing tool.
